hero.title: Water in the making
hero.subtitle: Explore the wastewater treatment plant of Béni Mellal.
hero.description: A close look at the infrastructure, units and processes involved in wastewater management.

media.alt: From a domestic tap to an underground pipe: opening sequence.

chapters.title: An everyday gesture
chapters.text: It all starts with an everyday gesture. After use, water enters an invisible but essential journey.
chapters.secondary: Kitchen, bathroom and toilet water: domestic wastewater carries fats, detergents, organic matter and germs.

media.alt: Water running from a tap into a basin.

chapters.title: An invisible journey
chapters.text: Under the streets of Béni Mellal, the sewer network collects wastewater and carries it to the treatment facilities.
chapters.secondary: The network serving Béni Mellal and Mghila is a combined system: domestic wastewater and rainwater flow together to the plant inlet.

media.alt: Inside an underground pipe with flowing water.

chapters.title: Arrival
chapters.text: At the end of the journey, the plant brings together units and equipment whose functions form a treatment line.
chapters.secondary: The plant covers about 18 ha, nearly 2 km from the city, along provincial road P3219.

media.alt: 3D model aerial view: circular trickling filters, basins, buildings and roads of the plant.

chapters.title: Understanding water
chapters.text: Understanding wastewater treatment also means better understanding the issues of water, the environment and territories.

components.name: Inlet and pretreatment
components.technicalName: Inlet structure, screening, lifting, metering, grit removal
components.shortDescription: The head of the plant: raw water is cleared of bulky waste and sand before any treatment.
components.role: Raw water first passes through coarse screening and then fine screening, which retain solid waste collected in a skip. It is then lifted, metered by a flow meter and de-gritted in a vortex grit chamber; the extracted sand goes through a classifier before removal.
components.details: A by-pass upstream of the screens can divert part of the flow during exceptional peaks or maintenance. In wet weather, the combined sewer network brings clay particles that increase the suspended solids load.

photos.caption: Screening.

photos.caption: Waste retained by screening.

photos.caption: Grit chamber.

photos.caption: Sand classifier.

components.note: No dedicated render of this unit is available yet.

components.name: Anaerobic basins
components.shortDescription: Four large basins in series where suspended solids settle and organic matter breaks down without oxygen.
components.role: The long retention time lets particles settle at the bottom of the basins. The particulate and organic load is reduced before biological treatment, which relieves the secondary stage.
components.details: Operation in series keeps treatment running when one basin is under maintenance. Settled sludge is sent to the drying beds.

photos.alt: Basin with a dark surface, edged with riprap.
photos.caption: Anaerobic basin.

photos.alt: View of a basin from the service track.

render.alt: Aerial render of the model: the basins of the plant.

components.note: The synoptic diagram calls them “anaerobic basins”; the visit report describes them as primary settling basins, and the GIS plan names them “Bassin de décantation primaire”.

components.name: Valve pit of the trickling filters
components.shortDescription: A technical pit where a main pipe branches into tappings fitted with valves.
components.role: Located next to the trickling filters (“LB”), the pit groups the main pipe, its tappings, the valves and the related electrical boxes.

photos.alt: Concrete pit with a galvanised pipe and a row of blue valves.
photos.caption: Pipe and valves in the pit.

render.alt: Model render: long pit with blue valves and gantries.

components.note: Its exact role in feeding the trickling filters is not detailed in the available documentation.

components.name: Trickling filters
components.shortDescription: Four circular towers where a bacterial biofilm breaks down dissolved organic matter.
components.role: Water is spread by a rotating distributor over a packing medium. Micro-organisms fixed on this medium as a biofilm break down organic matter in the presence of oxygen; part of it becomes water and carbon dioxide, the rest forms biomass removed as sludge.
components.details: Water passes through the filter very quickly, in a few minutes. Dosing conditions control how the biofilm detaches, and therefore the stability of the treatment.

photos.alt: Two large terracotta-coloured cylindrical towers.
photos.caption: The trickling filters seen from the road.

photos.alt: Top of a trickling filter: black packing and distributor arm.
photos.caption: Packing and distributor.

render.alt: Model render: four circular trickling filters surrounded by vegetation.

parameters.label: Feed
parameters.value: 16 pumps with protection filters and recycling valves

components.name: Clarifiers
components.shortDescription: Circular tanks where water separates from the sludge formed by biological treatment.
components.role: At rest, the sludge, heavier than water, settles at the bottom while a rotating bridge travels around the tank. Clarified water overflows the weir plates towards the next stage.
components.details: The line includes a sludge pumping station and a scum pumping station; the sludge is sent back to the anaerobic basins.

photos.alt: Circular clarifier with dark water, scraper bridge in the foreground.
photos.caption: Clarifier.

photos.alt: Notched weir plate around a clarifier.
photos.caption: Weir plate.

render.alt: Model render: clarifier and its rotating bridge.

components.note: The model and the GIS plan include three circular tanks in this group (two clarifiers and a small clarifier); the synoptic diagram shows two. The number and name of each remain to be confirmed.

components.name: Maturation ponds
components.shortDescription: Four large lagoons that refine the quality of the clarified water.
components.role: At the end of lagoon treatment, these ponds contribute to the disinfection of the effluent and reduce residual pollution, especially particulate and organic.
components.details: Their design aims to limit odours and to prevent plant growth on the banks, in order to reduce algae development.

photos.alt: Large calm lagoon edged with a riprap bank.
photos.caption: Maturation pond.

photos.alt: Riprap bank of a maturation pond, mountains in the background.

render.alt: Aerial render of the model: the maturation ponds.

components.name: Pumping station and analysers
components.shortDescription: Pumping, distribution and continuous water-quality measurement before tertiary treatment.
components.role: The visit report describes, upstream of tertiary treatment, a lifting station equipped with an ultrasonic flow meter and sensors that continuously measure turbidity, suspended solids, electrical conductivity and pH. These data are sent to the supervision system of the control centre.
components: Turbidity, SS, conductivity and pH sensors

photos.alt: Row of sheltered analysers, probes dipping into a channel.
photos.caption: Online analysers.

photos.alt: Analyser screen showing a reading.

render.alt: Model render: pumping station under a green steel frame.

components.note: The exact match between this part of the model and the “lifting station” of the report remains to be confirmed.

components.name: Coagulation, flocculation and filtration
components.shortDescription: The final polishing: the finest particles are clumped together and then retained by sand filters.
components.role: Ferric chloride (FeCl₃) and powdered activated carbon are injected to destabilise colloidal particles and adsorb micropollutants. The particles then gather into flocs, and the water passes through sand filters.
components.details: The sand filters are run in alternation so treatment continues while they are cleaned. Washing uses treated water; the dirty wash water is sent back to the head of the plant.

photos.alt: Stirred tank with green railings and mixer motor.
photos.caption: Tertiary treatment tanks.

photos.alt: Concrete channel with parallel troughs and foamy water.
Technical gallery with pipes and valves.

render.alt: Model render: filtration building and coagulators.

components.note: The attribution of each photograph to a specific tertiary unit remains to be checked.

components.name: UV area
components.shortDescription: Ultraviolet modules installed above a channel.
components.role: The visit photographs show UV modules placed on a channel. Ultraviolet radiation is one of the water disinfection methods mentioned in the visit report.

photos.alt: Stainless-steel UV modules on a channel, gratings around.
photos.caption: UV modules.

render.alt: Model render: low slab of the UV area.

components.note: The exact position of this step in the treatment line is not described in the available documentation.

components.name: Dirty wash water tank
components.shortDescription: It collects the water used to clean the sand filters.
components.role: Water from filter washing is collected here, then sent back upstream to the primary treatment to be treated again.

render.alt: Model render: rectangular dirty wash water tank.

components.name: Sludge drying beds
components.shortDescription: Sludge from settling is dewatered naturally here.
components.role: Sludge extracted from the anaerobic basins is spread here and loses its water by natural dewatering. It is then generally sent to the solid waste stream.

render.alt: Model render: sludge drying cells with cracked ground.

components.note: No photograph of this unit has been identified with certainty yet. The GIS plan counts 30 cells.

components.name: Control centre
components.shortDescription: The supervision post from which treatment is operated.
components.role: Sensor readings are transmitted here continuously. Tertiary treatment is operated from a control room equipped with electric valves, to manage flows and reagent doses.

photos.alt: Control room with workstations and a large window.

render.alt: Model render: control centre building with glazed balconies.

about.title: A model, a journey
about.text: This website is a digital visualization and interactive presentation project. It offers an educational reading of the Béni Mellal wastewater treatment plant based on a 3D model, visit photographs and the available documentation.
about.signature: 3D model and digital experience design: Ilyass Zerqtouni
about.disclaimer: The plant is a public facility whose design, construction and operation are the responsibility of its owners and operators. This website is not its official documentation: descriptions are educational and every technical statement refers to its source.
